title: Cloudflare Introduces Meerkat for Strongly Consistent Global Coordination
gist: Cloudflare has built Meerkat, an internal globally consistent control-plane service on the QuePaxa consensus algorithm, trading one-to-three round trips for leaderless writes that avoid the availability loss Raft suffers when a wide-area leader fails. It is not yet in production but has run proofs of concept with up to 50 worldwide replicas, and would be the first global-scale production deployment of QuePaxa.

insights.claim: Cloudflare has built Meerkat, an internal globally consistent control-plane service based on the QuePaxa consensus algorithm that allows leaderless writes while preserving strong consistency.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: A hyperscale edge operator moving off Raft signals that leader-based consensus is a live reliability constraint for global networks.
insights.locator: Cloudflare recently introduced Meerkat, an internal globally consistent control-plane service

insights.claim: Leader-based consensus algorithms such as Raft degrade in wide-area networks because a crashed or network-degraded leader makes the system unavailable until another replica times out and a new leader is elected.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Explains the mechanism behind repeated control-plane outages at globally distributed infrastructure providers.
insights.quote: The leader is the only replica allowed to make writes, and if it fails due to a crash or network degradation, the system becomes unavailable until some other replica times out and a new leader is elected.
insights.locator: Unfortunately, commonly deployed consensus algorithms like Raft

insights.claim: QuePaxa lets all replicas accept writes without relying on leader timeouts, removing the availability loss leader-based systems suffer when a leader becomes unreachable across wide-area networks.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: The design trade being made is availability-under-partition bought with extra round trips, not with weaker consistency.
insights.locator: Unlike Raft, QuePaxa allows all replicas to accept writes

insights.claim: Cloudflare says Meerkat is expected to be the first production deployment of QuePaxa at a global scale.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: First-mover production validation of an academic algorithm is the gating event for wider industry adoption.
insights.locator: Cloudflare says it is expected to be the first production deployment

insights.claim: QuePaxa is an asynchronous consensus algorithm, unlike Paxos and Raft which are partially synchronous and only make progress when message delay is small relative to timeout durations.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Asynchrony is the differentiator to watch: it makes progress survive wild message-delay fluctuations that break timeout-based systems.
insights.quote: QuePaxa doesn't rely on timeouts and makes progress even under wild fluctuations in message delay. The question is whether performance is competitive enough in the normal case.
insights.locator: In a popular Hacker News thread

insights.claim: Meerkat achieves strong consistency through a globally replicated consensus log in which all replicas agree on the order and values of committed operations, guaranteeing linearizable reads and writes.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Linearizable global state is what control planes need before they can safely coordinate leases and configuration across regions.
insights.locator: the article explains how Meerkat achieves strong consistency

insights.claim: The Meerkat log is a sequence of slots in which every slot except the last is decided, and its core invariant is that no two replicas ever disagree on the value of a decided slot.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: The slot invariant is the simple mental model for auditing whether a distributed control plane can diverge.
insights.quote: One of Meerkat’s invariants is that if any two replicas decide on the value for a slot, those values are the same.
insights.locator: The Meerkat log is a sequence of slots

insights.claim: Meerkat's consensus log is built to support higher-level services including a transactional key-value store and a leasing system.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Leasing plus a transactional KV store is exactly the primitive set needed to coordinate global edge configuration.
insights.locator: Meerkat provides a consensus log that supports services

insights.claim: QuePaxa usually takes one to three round trips between the initial proposer and a majority of replicas to decide on a proposal and append an event to the log, and can take more.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Round-trip count is the hard cost ceiling that decides which workloads can sit on this consensus layer.
insights.quote: QuePaxa in particular takes one to three round trips (usually, although it can take more) between the initial proposer and a majority of replicas to decide on a proposal and add an event to the log.

insights.claim: Cloudflare explicitly scopes Meerkat away from general-purpose data systems such as databases, positioning it only as coordination infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Rules out the read of this as a database product launch; it is internal control-plane plumbing.
insights.quote: Meerkat has limitations. It is not designed to create general-purpose data systems like databases.

insights.claim: Consensus overhead typically adds 40-60% latency in multi-region Paxos deployments, per research cited by KPIT software engineer Aniket Ray, which is why latency optimization is critical for strongly consistent systems.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Quantifies the tax on strong consistency across regions and sets the bar Meerkat must clear to be adopted.
insights.quote: Research shows consensus overhead typically adds 40-60% latency in multi-region Paxos deployments, making Meerkat's optimization critical for strongly consistent systems.
insights.locator: While some developers ask Cloudflare to open source the specification

insights.claim: Meerkat is not yet deployed to production, but Cloudflare has completed multiple proofs of concept with up to 50 replicas distributed worldwide.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Pre-production status means the availability benefit is unproven; the 50-replica PoC scale is the milestone to track.
insights.quote: Meerkat is not yet deployed to production, but Cloudflare says it has completed multiple proofs of concept with up to 50 replicas distributed worldwide.
insights.locator: Meerkat is not yet deployed to production

insights.claim: Practitioners in a popular Hacker News thread found Cloudflare's write-up hard to follow and questioned whether the additional round trips are worth it in typical deployments, and some asked Cloudflare to open source the design and verification specification.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Community skepticism plus a closed specification slows the path from one vendor's deployment to an industry standard.
insights.locator: In a popular Hacker News thread
